clue.text: Dismissed editor from corrupt Scots town

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so that person is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: corrupt in the sense of evil or sinful
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is sacked after a scandal at a crooked council in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ED out of WICKED to leave WICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a small coastal town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland.

clue.text: Bowl short? That's a relief

blocks.note: a wood is a bowl in the game of bowls
short in the sense of cut down

explanation.surface: A bowler's delivery falls short, and someone sighs with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a relief' is not an exclamation but a definition: a relief is a kind of print.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a relief print made from a block where the uncut raised parts take the ink.

clue.text: About to change belief

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to redo something is to change it

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of changing what they believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of the principles a person holds true.

clue.text: Clothes son obtained in return

indicators.note: something in return comes back the other way, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
obtained means got

explanation.surface: A son is given some clothes in exchange for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is informal British slang for garments, especially ones worn for a particular activity.

clue.text: Fur company put up English item for sale

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up writes it bottom to top, the opposite way

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
E is the abbreviation for English
a lot is an item offered at auction

explanation.surface: A furrier puts up an English item at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocelot is a spotted wild cat whose pelt was once prized as fur.

clue.text: Feature of bay and another horse in South-East

indicators.note: pieces placed in another are put inside it, between its letters

blocks.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
taken as written
a dun is a greyish-brown horse, as a bay is a reddish-brown one

explanation.surface: A bay horse and another of a different colour stand in the South-East.
explanation.walkthrough: Bay reads as a horse colour, which is why the clue says 'another horse'; for the definition it is a stretch of coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand dune is a ridge of windblown sand, often found along the shore of a bay.

clue.text: Whiter fence made by such a person?

definitions.text: fence made by such a person?

blocks.note: first meaning: more pale in colour

blocks.clueFragment: fence made by such a person?
blocks.note: second meaning: a pale is a fence stake, so a fence builder could jokingly be one who makes pales

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful coinage: a pale is a fence or a stake in one, so a person who puts up pales would be a PALER. The question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Paler is the comparative of pale, meaning lighter in colour and so closer to white.

clue.text: One page in history piece that could be written

definitions.note: the definition is by example: written is one

indicators.note: the pieces named first are placed in what follows, between its letters

blocks.note: history is the past
a particle is a tiny piece
I is the Roman numeral for one
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A single page of a history book that someone might write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written' is quoted as a word, not a description of the page: it is an example of the grammatical form.
explanation.definitionFit: Written is the past participle of the verb write, so the answer names its grammatical form.

clue.text: Pedestrian mug a new driver upset promises to settle scores

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down so they are read from the bottom

blocks.note: to mug someone is to rob them
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A walker attacks a learner driver, who promises to get even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker; it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Laborious writing is heavy and plodding, just as pedestrian prose is dull and uninspired.

clue.text: Right way out of lapse

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: The correct route for escaping a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' belongs with 'way out': an egress is a way out of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to slip back to a worse or earlier state, as to lapse is.

clue.text: Dreadful sensation produced by Titanic disaster?

blocks.note: first meaning: the lurch of dismay when something has gone wrong
second meaning, taken literally: what those aboard felt as the liner went down

explanation.surface: The horror felt by those caught up in the loss of the Titanic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal second reading: a ship going under gives a feeling of going down with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinking feeling is the dismayed sense that something has gone badly wrong, and the ship literally sank.

clue.text: Former individual contribution to this paper?

blocks.note: an individual is one person
this paper is The Times, and the letters given here form most of its name, a part contributed to it

explanation.surface: A single writer's piece once printed in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This paper' is The Times, where the puzzle was printed; TIME is the bulk of its title, so it is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time is an adjective meaning former or erstwhile, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Horse eats to live, so put back this?

definitions.text: Horse eats to live, so put back this?

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the letters before it are read in reverse order
what eats takes the other words inside itself

blocks.note: to live is to be
taken as written
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse needs to eat to stay alive, so you hang this on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, so it doubles as the definition: a horse must eat, hence the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feed bag hung over a horse's head so it can eat; the clue is the reason one is fitted.

clue.text: Revs have to be kept within this?

definitions.text: Revs have to be kept within this?

blocks.clueFragment: Revs have to be kept within this?
blocks.note: surface reading: an engine's revolutions held within some limit or machine, as with a car

blocks.clueFragment: Revs have to be kept within this?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Revs are clergymen (Reverends), and all Anglican clergy are listed in one reference book

explanation.surface: Engine revs must stay inside a certain range or vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rev is the short form of Reverend; Crockford's Clerical Directory lists Church of England clergy. A crock and a Ford are also both cars, which fits the engine reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockford is the standard directory naming every Anglican clergyman, so Reverends are recorded inside it.

clue.text: Shilling found in simple money bag

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: simple in the sense of unmixed or plain
S is the abbreviation for shilling, the old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: A coin turns up inside a plain little moneybag.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a small bag for carrying coins and other money.

clue.text: Skill is something that can go off when imbibing drink

indicators.note: one that is imbibing takes the drink into itself, so it wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: TNT is an explosive, which goes off
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Talent sounds like something that spoils once you have had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' suggests turning sour, like milk; here it means exploding.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural aptitude or ability, the same as a skill.

clue.text: A way round county river for squire?

indicators.note: something put round another encloses it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: a lane is a way or road
Down is a county in Northern Ireland
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A road circling a county and its river leads to the squire's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire was the chief owner of land in an English village or district.

clue.text: Titanic's no more, wrecked going to America

indicators.note: a wreck is broken up, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: The famous liner sank on her way to America and is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' reads as the ship, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic as an adjective means gigantic, of the size of the mythical Titans.

clue.text: The last character to love work they arranged? Sponge, perhaps

indicators.note: things arranged are put in order, so these letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
OP is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dramatist's final character loves the work the cast arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoophyte is an old term for invertebrate animals that look like plants, such as sponges and corals.

clue.text: Fare on boat from China?

blocks.note: surface reading: meals served aboard a ship sailing from China
setter's reading: a Chinese sailing boat has a name that also means rubbish, and its fare is unhealthy food

explanation.surface: What passengers eat on a voyage from China.
explanation.walkthrough: A junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing ship, so its food is literally junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk food is cheap, unhealthy fast fare; fare here means food rather than a ticket price.

clue.text: Beast of burden has to lift a vessel

blocks.note: to jack something up is to lift it
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A pack animal must haul a boat up out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey, a traditional animal for carrying loads.

clue.text: Find in Miami a small pollution problem

indicators.note: you are told to find the answer inside the words that follow, which conceal it

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A minor smog issue turns up in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious, polluting vapour, once thought to cause disease.

clue.text: Misbehaving by lamas is unusual

indicators.note: behaving badly means not keeping in line, so the letters break their order

blocks.note: the letters of the two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour by Buddhist monks is a rare thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: lamas behaving badly would be dreadful, and rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly bad, a fair word for monks misbehaving.

clue.text: Excellent pals?

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
the question mark flags a hidden instruction: in a down light the word is written upwards

explanation.walkthrough: The answer itself is the instruction: PALS written up a down light reads SLAP, so it is 'pals' going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-up is informal British for lavish and first-rate, as in a slap-up meal.

clue.text: Fail to get ventilation in church right

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
a variant spelling of OK, meaning all right

explanation.surface: A stuffy church leaves the congregation short of air.
explanation.walkthrough: OKE is an old variant spelling of OK, as in okey-doke.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke is to be unable to breathe, failing to take in enough air.

clue.text: Telling fortune of friend seeing obscurity with lines

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
mist obscures things
RY is the abbreviation for railway, and railway lines are lines

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant friend peers through the fog at the lines on a palm.
explanation.walkthrough: The lines also fit the surface: palmists read the lines of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is the practice of predicting someone's future by reading the creases of the hand.

clue.text: Stuff from voyage to the Orient

blocks.note: a voyage is a trip
E is east, the direction of the Orient

explanation.surface: Goods brought back from a journey to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' reads as goods; it means nonsense, as in 'stuff and nonsense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is worthless talk or rubbish, and stuff can mean nonsense too.

clue.text: A night in Paris, in no particular pension

indicators.note: one piece placed in another goes inside it, here between its letters

blocks.note: any means no particular one
une nuit is French for a night

explanation.surface: Spending a night in Paris on no particular pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A night in Paris' reads as a holiday, but it asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed yearly payment, often bought to provide a retirement income.

clue.text: More marks needed to secure everyone an ancient garment

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the outer pieces wrap around another

blocks.note: più is the Italian musical direction for more
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Extra marks are needed to win a prize for an old robe.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical scores use più, Italian for more; marks were the German currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallium was a cloak worn by men in ancient Greece and Rome, and is still a church vestment.

clue.text: Call for silence before game and note a gesture of apathy

blocks.note: sh is said to call for quiet
RU stands for Rugby Union
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A referee hushes the crowd before the match, and notices someone indifferent.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug lifts the shoulders briefly to show that the person does not care or know.

clue.text: See, with sixth sense, the unknown

blocks.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is called the sixth sense
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A psychic sees what nobody knows through a sixth sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, a literary verb for spotting.

clue.text: Genuine noble runs to the front

indicators.note: a letter sent to the front leaves its old place and is set at the start instead

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A true aristocrat hurries to the head of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of EARL moves from its end to its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Real means actual or authentic, the opposite of fake.
